questions.q: When starting a full-stack Microsoft BI capstone project, why is it important to define the end reports/dashboards you need before building the warehouse schema?
options: Working backward from the actual reporting needs ensures the fact/dimension grain and attributes you build actually support the questions the business needs answered
The order doesn't matter as long as everything is built eventually
SSRS requires the warehouse to be built first by law
Power BI can build its own warehouse automatically
questions.explain: A warehouse built without a clear picture of the reports it needs to support risks the wrong grain or missing attributes — starting from what questions the business needs answered and working backward into the model is what keeps the whole stack coherent.

questions.q: In a full Microsoft BI capstone, what's the typical high-level data flow across the stack?
options: Source systems, then SSIS for ETL, into a data warehouse star schema, then SSRS paginated reports and Power BI dashboards
Power BI first, then SSIS extracts from Power BI
SSRS is the source system for the warehouse
Source systems connect directly to Power BI with no warehouse or ETL involved
questions.explain: The Microsoft BI stack's conventional flow moves data from raw source systems, through SSIS for extraction/transformation, into a properly modeled warehouse, which both SSRS and Power BI then serve reports and dashboards from — each tool at its correct layer.

questions.q: If a capstone's SSIS package loads a Type 2 slowly changing Customer dimension, and the Power BI model sums SalesAmount by Customer, what could go wrong if the fact table's CustomerKey wasn't loaded correctly against the SCD's surrogate key?
options: Sales could get attributed to the wrong version of a customer's history, or fail to match any dimension row at all, producing missing or misleading totals
Nothing — Power BI automatically corrects mismatched keys
The measure would simply run slower but stay correct
SSIS would refuse to run the package entirely
questions.explain: This is exactly why fact-to-dimension key integrity matters end to end — a fact row pointing at the wrong, or no, surrogate key silently misattributes or drops that row from totals sliced by customer, with no error thrown anywhere in the stack.

questions.q: Why would a capstone project's SSRS paginated report and Power BI dashboard often be built against the same warehouse tables rather than each having its own separate data pull?
options: Reusing the same governed warehouse tables keeps both tools' numbers consistent with each other, a single source of truth
Power BI can't connect to a data warehouse
SSRS requires its own dedicated copy of every table
It's not possible for two BI tools to share one warehouse
questions.explain: If SSRS and Power BI each pulled their own separate copy or interpretation of the data, small differences in filtering or logic could make the two tools' numbers disagree — building both against the same warehouse tables is what keeps a single source of truth real in practice.

questions.q: In the full stack, what's the role of the SSIS-built ETL layer relative to the T-SQL skills learned earlier in the program?
options: SSIS orchestrates the overall extract/transform/load workflow, but individual steps, such as an Execute SQL Task or a stored procedure call, still rely directly on T-SQL
T-SQL is no longer needed once SSIS is introduced
SSIS replaces the need to know T-SQL entirely
T-SQL is only used for reporting, never ETL
questions.explain: SSIS is a workflow and data-movement tool — it very often calls out to real T-SQL, such as stored procedures or MERGE statements, to do the actual set-based data work, so the T-SQL foundation stays directly relevant inside the ETL layer, not replaced by it.

questions.q: A capstone dashboard shows a KPI that doesn't match a paginated report built from the "same" data. What's the first thing to check?
options: Whether the two reports are actually using the same filter context, grain, and time period, not just the same table
Immediately assume Power BI has a bug
Rebuild the entire warehouse from scratch
Delete one of the two reports
questions.explain: Mismatched numbers between two reports built on "the same" data are almost always a filter, grain, or date-range mismatch rather than a platform bug — checking assumptions first saves a lot of wasted rebuilding.

questions.q: Why does a capstone project typically ask you to add basic error handling/logging to the SSIS load, even for a student project?
options: It mirrors what a real production job actually requires, and demonstrates the practice to an interviewer or hiring manager reviewing the portfolio
Error handling is only relevant to enterprise-scale projects
SSIS packages can't run at all without it
It's purely a formality graded on effort, not real skill
questions.explain: A capstone is a portfolio piece — showing that you build packages the way a real production job would, with error handling and logging, not just a happy-path load, is exactly the kind of judgment a hiring manager is trying to assess.

questions.q: If the warehouse's Date dimension is missing the current year's dates, what specifically breaks first, downstream?
options: Any fact rows dated this year can't find a matching Date dimension row, and time-intelligence measures like year-over-year built on that Date table will be wrong or blank
Power BI Desktop will fail to open the file
SSRS will refuse to render any report at all
SSIS will overwrite the missing dates automatically at next refresh
questions.explain: This is a direct, practical consequence of the Date-dimension concepts from the warehousing course — a fact row can't join to a Date dimension row that doesn't exist, and DAX time-intelligence functions specifically depend on that calendar being complete.

questions.q: When integrating Power Query with a warehouse that already has clean, modeled star-schema tables, how much transformation logic should typically remain in Power Query?
options: Very little — most cleaning/shaping should already have happened in the ETL/warehouse layer; Power Query should mainly just connect and lightly adapt for reporting needs
All transformation logic belongs in Power Query regardless of what the warehouse already does
Power Query should rebuild the warehouse's star schema from scratch every time
It doesn't matter where transformation logic lives
questions.explain: Putting heavy transformation logic in Power Query on top of an already-modeled warehouse duplicates work and creates two places logic can drift apart — if the ETL layer already did the real cleaning and shaping, Power Query's job is mostly just to connect and layer on report-specific needs.

questions.q: Why is source control, such as Git, recommended even for a single-developer BI capstone project?
options: It gives you a real history of changes and a safety net to revert to a working version, and demonstrates a practice every real BI team expects
Git is only useful with multiple developers
SSIS and Power BI files can't be stored in Git
It replaces the need for backups of the database itself
questions.explain: Even solo, source control gives you the ability to see what changed and roll back a bad change — and using it on a portfolio project signals to an employer that you already work the way a real team does.

questions.q: What's a reasonable production practice for handling a scheduled SSIS job that fails partway through the night?
options: Alerting on failure plus a re-runnable, idempotent load design, so someone finds out quickly and re-running doesn't create duplicate or corrupted data
Ignoring failures since the job will just try again automatically with no side effects
Manually checking every morning with no automated alert at all
Disabling the schedule permanently after any single failure
questions.explain: Production ETL needs two things working together: you actually find out something failed, through alerting, and re-running the failed load doesn't make things worse, through idempotency — relying on either alone leaves a real gap.

questions.q: Why would a real BI team document a data dictionary as part of "finishing" a project, not as optional extra work?
options: Without it, new team members, or the original developer months later, have to reverse-engineer meaning from column names and guesswork, which is slow and error-prone
Data dictionaries are only required for regulatory compliance
SQL Server auto-generates documentation with no extra effort
Documentation is only useful for SSRS reports, not warehouses
questions.explain: A warehouse's real value is in being understood and trusted by people beyond its original builder — a data dictionary is what keeps a cryptic column's meaning from being a mystery six months later.

questions.q: When presenting this capstone project in a job interview, why is walking through your design decisions usually more valuable than just showing the finished dashboard?
options: Interviewers are assessing your judgment and reasoning process, not just whether the final output looks polished
Interviewers only care about visual design
Design decisions are considered confidential and shouldn't be discussed
The finished dashboard alone always tells the complete story
questions.explain: A polished dashboard demonstrates output, but walking through why you chose a particular grain, or SCD type, or ETL pattern demonstrates the actual engineering judgment a BI Developer role is hiring for — which is what technical interviewers are usually really probing for.

questions.q: What's a strong way to frame this program's capstone on a resume, versus just listing "completed Microsoft BI Developer training"?
options: Describe the concrete stack and outcome, such as "Built an end-to-end SQL Server/SSIS/SSRS/Power BI pipeline modeling a star-schema warehouse and dashboard"
List only the course title with no further detail
Omit the capstone from the resume since it wasn't a paid job
List every single lesson title from the course
questions.explain: Concrete, specific accomplishment statements read far more credibly to a hiring manager than a generic training-completion line — it's the difference between "took a course" and "can point to something built."

questions.q: In a technical interview for a BI Developer role, why might you be asked to explain the difference between WHERE and HAVING, or Type 1 vs. Type 2 SCDs, rather than just asked to write a full ETL pipeline live?
options: Interviewers often test fundamentals precisely because they reveal whether your understanding is solid, not just whether you can follow a tutorial
Fundamentals questions are meaningless filler with no real signal
Only senior candidates are ever asked fundamentals questions
These questions are asked purely to make candidates uncomfortable
questions.explain: A candidate who can build along with a tutorial but can't explain why a HAVING clause exists, or what problem a Type 2 SCD solves, hasn't fully internalized the material — fundamentals questions are a fast, reliable way for an interviewer to check for that gap.

questions.q: What's the value of a portfolio, such as a repo with your capstone's SQL scripts, SSIS package, and a Power BI report screenshot, alongside a resume?
options: It gives a hiring manager concrete evidence of your actual work, not just a claim on paper
Portfolios are only relevant for software engineering roles, never BI roles
A resume alone is always sufficient proof of skill
Portfolios should never include real code, only descriptions
questions.explain: Anyone can write "proficient in SSIS" on a resume — a portfolio with real, inspectable work is what actually backs that claim up for a hiring manager deciding who to interview.

questions.q: Why is it worth preparing a specific, honest answer for "what would you do differently" about your own capstone project, before an interview?
options: It shows self-awareness and the ability to critically evaluate your own work, a trait interviewers specifically look for
It's a trick question with no good answer
Admitting any flaw in your project will disqualify you
The capstone should be presented as flawless with no room for improvement
questions.explain: A candidate who can honestly and specifically reflect on what they'd improve demonstrates real engineering maturity — interviewers are generally more impressed by thoughtful self-critique than by a claim that nothing could be improved.

questions.q: Why should salary research, using real current postings, happen before a job offer negotiation, not after?
options: Knowing the real current market range for the role and region before you're in the conversation lets you negotiate from an informed position rather than reacting in the moment
Salary research is unnecessary once you have any offer at all
Negotiating is discouraged for entry-level roles
Employers set salary ranges that can never be negotiated
questions.explain: Walking into a negotiation without knowing the going market rate means reacting to whatever number is offered rather than anchoring the conversation with real information — research done ahead of time is what makes an informed negotiation possible.

questions.q: After completing this capstone, what's the recommended next step this catalog frames as optional rather than required?
options: Adding a specialization, like Python, Tableau, or a cloud data engineering track, once you're already employable with this foundation
Repeating the entire T-SQL course from scratch before applying to any jobs
Waiting a full year before applying for any BI Developer roles
Avoiding applying to jobs until every possible Microsoft certification is completed
questions.explain: The Microsoft Data & BI Developer path is designed as a complete, employable foundation on its own — additional specializations are explicitly framed as something to add later, once you're already working, not a prerequisite to getting the first job.

questions.q: What's the main reason this program frames "no job guarantee, but real production-pattern skills" as the honest value proposition, rather than promising a job?
options: Overpromising outcomes nobody can actually control undermines trust; demonstrating real, job-relevant skill and judgment is what's actually within the program's and the student's control
Promising a job outright always increases enrollment with no downside
It's a legal requirement to include a disclaimer
This framing only applies to unpaid programs
questions.explain: A training program can't control an individual hiring outcome, but it can make sure what's taught actually reflects how the work gets done in a real job — being honest about that distinction, rather than overpromising, is the more trustworthy claim to make.
